presentingComplaint: 3 days of worsening breathlessness with increased sputum volume and change to green colour
history: 68-year-old man with a 45 pack-year smoking history and GOLD group E COPD (FEV1 48% predicted, two exacerbations last year) presents with 3 days of progressive breathlessness beyond his baseline, increased sputum volume, and a change from clear to purulent green sputum. Preceded by coryzal symptoms. Reduced exercise tolerance from 200 m to a few steps. Home therapy is a LABA/LAMA/ICS inhaler and PRN salbutamol, now needing near-hourly. No orthopnoea, PND, chest pain, or haemoptysis. Ex-farmer, lives with wife, on home oxygen 1 L/min at night.
examination: Alert but breathless, using accessory muscles and pursed-lip breathing, speaking in short sentences. Barrel chest, hyperresonant percussion, prolonged expiratory phase with diffuse polyphonic wheeze and scattered coarse crepitations. Mild ankle oedema. Pertinent negatives: no focal consolidation dullness, no unilateral leg swelling/calf tenderness, no raised JVP suggestive of decompensated cor pulmonale, no asterixis, no fever.

labs.ABG (room air): pH 7.36, PaCO2 6.4 kPa, PaO2 8.1 kPa, HCO3 27 mmol/L

imaging: CXR: hyperinflated lung fields with flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation, pneumothorax or effusion - excludes pneumonia/pneumothorax as alternative causes.
microbiology: Sputum culture sent (commonly H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, M. catarrhalis; Pseudomonas if frequent exacerbations/prior isolation); blood cultures if febrile - pending.
differentialDiagnoses: Acute decompensated heart failure / pulmonary oedema
finalDiagnosis: Acute infective exacerbation of COPD (all three Anthonisen cardinal symptoms present)
stewardship: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate (or doxycycline) empirically, indicated because all three Anthonisen cardinal symptoms (increased dyspnoea, sputum volume, and sputum purulence) are present; reserve anti-pseudomonal cover (e.g. ciprofloxacin) for those with prior Pseudomonas isolation or frequent exacerbations. Cornerstone treatment is controlled oxygen (target SpO2 88-92%), nebulised bronchodilators, and systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone 40 mg x5 days).
contraindications: Penicillin allergy - substitute doxycycline or a macrolide
Avoid high-flow uncontrolled oxygen: risk of CO2 narcosis in chronic hypercapnia; titrate to 88-92%
edgeCases: Hypercapnic respiratory failure (pH <7.35 with rising PaCO2) requiring NIV - do not miss
Eosinophilic exacerbation phenotype predicts steroid responsiveness
Overlap with heart failure or PE - pulmonary embolism found in a notable minority of exacerbations without clear cause
expectedMaiK: Classic infective COPD exacerbation with all three Anthonisen cardinal symptoms, justifying empiric antibiotics plus systemic steroids and controlled oxygen; watch for hypercapnic respiratory failure needing NIV and titrate O2 to 88-92%.

regressionAssertions: empiric antibiotics recommended only when Anthonisen cardinal symptoms / sputum purulence present
